questions.q: What four AdventureWorks2012 tables did the Lesson 3 query join together?
options: Sales.SalesOrderDetail, Sales.SalesOrderHeader, Production.Product, Sales.SalesTerritory
Sales.Customer, Sales.SalesOrderHeader, HumanResources.Employee, Production.Product
Production.Product, Production.ProductCategory, Sales.Store, Person.Person
Sales.SalesOrderDetail, Sales.SalesTerritory, Sales.Customer, Person.Address
questions.explain: These four tables supplied, respectively, the sales amounts, the order date and territory ID, the product line, and the readable territory name.

questions.q: According to the lesson's skills table, what is the real, transferable skill underlying Lessons 5 through 7 (visuals, DAX, formatting)?
options: Designing for a specific reader, not a generic audience
Translating a question into correct, efficient data retrieval
Delivering work in a form someone else can actually use
Requirements clarification
questions.explain: The DAX measures, slicer, and formatting choices were all shaped around what the Southeast manager specifically needed to read quickly — that's the underlying skill, not the tool mechanics.

questions.q: Which of these was deliberately left OUT of this Beginner capstone project?
options: SSIS, SSRS, a data warehouse, and a year-over-year trend comparison
A T-SQL query against AdventureWorks2012
DAX measures for total sales and order count
Publishing the report to the Power BI Service
questions.explain: The project was intentionally scoped to one quarter, one stakeholder, and T-SQL plus Power BI only — SSIS, SSRS, a warehouse, and trend analysis were explicitly out of scope.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe 'knowing how to scope down' as a real skill, not a limitation to apologize for?
options: Matching the project's effort to the actual size of the request was the correct choice, not a shortcut taken due to limited ability
Scoping down is only necessary when a company lacks the budget for SSIS or SSRS licenses
A smaller scope always produces a more accurate T-SQL query
The stakeholder specifically required SSIS and SSRS to be excluded
questions.explain: The request was for a quick quarterly snapshot; building a data warehouse or a multi-year trend for it would have mismatched effort to the actual ask, not demonstrated more skill.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does the Intermediate project add that this Beginner project deliberately avoided?
options: More stakeholders and a comparison across time, requiring the report to hold up under more scrutiny than a two-minute glance
Replacing T-SQL with a different query language entirely
Removing the need for requirements clarification
Building the report without any DAX measures at all
questions.explain: The Intermediate project raises the stakes in exactly the directions this Beginner project scoped out: more stakeholders and a time-based comparison, while still relying on the same foundational skills.
